Baseline `go test ./internal/sprint ./internal/app` green; `go test -race` green over the full review suite. Findings below; every candidate was traced through callers, guards, and tests, and the headline finding was reproduced empirically with an overlay-injected regression test (no target files touched; probe preserved as `evidence-probe-test.go.txt`). Note: the context pack referenced older commit `8eef70f`; all line numbers below were re-verified against `c6f01cf`. Environment observation (not a finding): during this session, `internal/workspace/skills.go` in the target checkout acquired an unrelated substantive modification (mtime 09:55:35Z, policy-text rewrite of execute-skill rules). This reviewer made no writes to the target tree (all probing via `go test -overlay` from `/tmp/opencode/probe`, see `overlay.json` alongside the probe); the change most likely comes from a concurrent actor sharing the checkout. Left untouched. --- ## F1 — Placeholder-substring gate deterministically fails valid reviews whose findings mention "TODO"/"TBD" (or whose input paths contain them); the stage then cannot complete while honest findings persist **Severity: medium-high · Confidence: very high (empirically reproduced)** **Claim.** `ValidateReviewContent` applies `containsPlaceholder` (index.go:218-221) to the entire rendered review.md, and `containsPlaceholder` flags any case-insensitive substring `todo` or `tbd` anywhere. RenderReviewMarkdown embeds model-authored finding titles/details/actions and diagnostic messages verbatim (review.go:1094-1105, 1106-1113). So a fully schema-valid, citation-valid reviewer result whose text mentions a TODO marker — arguably the single most canonical code-review finding — makes the finished review fail self-validation AFTER all reviewers ran and after the verdict ladder already computed `pass_with_findings`. **Observable bad outcome (reproduced).** With two reviewers returning valid results whose finding detail reads "…contains a todo comment…", `Review` returns `status=failed verdict=pass_with_findings err="generated review.md failed validation"`, diagnostic `artifact-invalid: empty or placeholder review`; review.md is never written; flow-state records a failed attempt. Control run with marker "followup-note" completes normally (`status=completed verdict=pass_with_findings`). Because finding text is regenerated per run, reruns reproduce the failure whenever reviewers keep reporting the TODO — a deterministic availability trap for any codebase that actually contains TODO comments (execute-stage output routinely does; target code is agent-authored). Second-order effect: the same validator runs inside `VerificationStatus` over stored artifacts (verify.go:197-199), so any such content that ever lands flags the whole verification assessment malformed/blocked until a luckier phrasing lands. **Trigger/preconditions.** Any of: finding title/detail/action, coverage summary, diagnostic message, changed-path or governed-input path containing substrings `todo`/`tbd` (paths are rendered in the Input Fingerprint section), or a `{{token}}`-style string quoted inside finding text. No attacker needed; ordinary developer content suffices. (A malicious governed input can also deliberately steer reviewers into the trap.) **Evidence / path.** 1. review.go:629-634 — `content := RenderReviewMarkdown(m, result)`; `if vf := ValidateReviewContent(content, m); len(vf) > 0 { … persistReviewFailure("generated review.md failed validation") }`. 2. index.go:218-221 — `strings.Contains(lower, "todo") || strings.Contains(lower, "tbd") || …`. 3. review.go:1094-1105 — findings rendered verbatim; 1083-1089 — input paths and changed paths rendered. 4. Reproduction: `GAUNTLET_MARKER=todo go test -overlay … -run TestGauntletMarkerFindingCompletion` → failed/artifact-invalid (see `evidence-probe-test.go.txt`); control marker → completed/pass_with_findings. 5. Contract context: TRD §18.6 does require review.md to contain "no placeholders", but the intent is unrendered-template detection (cf. planning validators); rejecting organic reviewer prose about real TODOs defeats the protocol's own requirement that actionable deviations be reported with citations (review-sprint-protocol; renderReviewerPrompt instructs findings to carry real citations). **Controls/counter-evidence searched.** No sanitization strips these substrings before render (`safeReviewText` redacts secrets/roots only). No test covers placeholder text inside findings — the `artifact-invalid` branch is untested and unreachable via the blocked path (blocked verdicts persist before render), which is why the trap survived. Result-level validation (`reviewResultProblems`) has no placeholder rule, proving acceptance upstream and rejection only at artifact level. Not fixable by operators short of rephrasing model outputs. **Regression test.** The attached probe: reviewer emits otherwise-valid low-severity direct finding mentioning "TODO"; assert `Review` completes and review.md passes `ValidateReviewContent`. Product fix options: restrict the final-artifact placeholder check to structural markers (template braces / literal ``) rather than English substrings, or apply it only to product-owned boilerplate sections, not model-authored text. --- ## F2 — Completed-review session deletion targets the wrong database; scoped runtime stores and `.ultra/cache/review` snapshots are reclaimed only by a sweep that finished sprints never trigger **Severity: low-medium · Confidence: high (mechanism verified end-to-end)** **Claim.** After success, `Review` deletes each completed session via `deleteCompletedSession` (review.go:657-659). For the production adapter this executes `agentwrap db "DELETE FROM event_sequence WHERE aggregate_id=…"` and `agentwrap session delete ` with env `append(os.Environ(), c.Agentwrap.Env...)` — no `OPENCODE_DB` (internal/platform/runtime/opencode.go:93-125, 180-184). But review sessions are created inside per-coverage scoped stores selected precisely by injecting `OPENCODE_DB` per request (service.go:1137-1139 → runtime.go:576-581 → agentwrap opencode/runtime.go:155-159). Deletion therefore runs against the default/global database, where these sessions do not exist: best-effort swallowed (`_ =`), it reclaims nothing while performing destructive SQL/VACUUM against an unrelated shared DB. **Observable bad outcome.** Every successful review leaves up to N retained stores (`projects/

/sprints//.ultraplan/runtime/opencode//opencode.db` with full transcripts) plus a complete `.ultra/cache/review/

///` snapshot copy. Reclamation depends solely on `CleanupRuntimeStores(sp.Path, 72h, 2GiB)` (runtime_metrics.go:119), which fires only when the NEXT runtime call admits work in that sprint — and snapshots are removed only on success (review.go:652), never on fail/cancel/blocked/crash paths. A sprint that ends after review leaks its stores and orphaned snapshot dirs (one per historical fingerprint) indefinitely; multi-sprint workspaces accumulate them without bound. **Trigger/preconditions.** Any completed review (stores); any failed/interrupted review or any superseded fingerprint (snapshots). **Evidence / path.** As cited above; store expiry conditions at store.go:211-227 require a subsequent `startSprintRuntime` call; snapshot removal only at review.go:652 (success) and rebuild-reset at 1613 (missing marker only). **Controls/counter-evidence searched.** `flow.go:37-42 deleteCompletedSessions` prefers whole-store deletion via `RuntimeStorePath` — but `Review` never uses it because completion state records sessions, not store paths. Errors being swallowed hides the mismatch. No TTL job exists for either location (grep across `internal/`). Verdict-fail intentionally retains sessions (review.go:654-656), compounding retention. **Regression test.** Adapter-level test: create a session under a scoped store (metadata `opencode.database_path`), call `DeleteSession`, assert rows removed from THAT database. Service-level test: after successful review with a fake deleter capturing the requested DB identity, assert deletion addresses the scoped store; add a lifecycle test asserting snapshot removal (or sweep) on terminal non-success outcomes. --- ## F3 — gitpublish failure after durable completion leaves review "completed" with no republication path; flow-level retry becomes a silent no-op and CLI retry pays a full fan-out **Severity: low · Confidence: high mechanism, medium impact** **Claim.** Terminal sequencing writes the artifact, then records completion durably (`saveReviewState(completed)`, clearing Resume and pinning digest/verdict), and only then publishes (review.go:636-651). If `publishReviewStage` fails, `Review` returns the error but durable state is already completed-with-matching-digest. Retry asymmetry follows: (a) `flow --to smoke`/`verify` treat the review as current (`currentReview := status.Review.Fresh && ExecutionStatus==completed…`, verify.go:65) and skip Review entirely — and unlike planning stages, which opportunistically republish on every flow pass (flow.go:149-155), there is no review republication outside `Review` itself; (b) the CLI `sprint … review` retry re-runs the entire bounded fan-out because Resume was cleared on the completed save, even though nothing about inputs changed. **Observable bad outcome.** Transient publisher failure (lock contention, hook rejection) yields a locally-complete review whose publication commit is missing from history; downstream flow operations proceed without it and never heal it; the operator's only cheap-looking remedy (`flow --to smoke`) silently does nothing, and the effective remedy re-spends every reviewer call. **Evidence / path.** review.go:644-651 ordering; verify.go:62-80 skip logic; flow.go:147-157 planning-stage republication asymmetry; resume cleared at review.go:1269. **Counter-evidence searched.** Direct CLI `review` rerun does republish — so recovery exists, but at full fan-out cost; smoke publishes harness/workspace paths but not `review.md` (publication.go:99-121). Digest/fingerprint checks make the local state self-consistent, so nothing detects the missing publication. **Regression test.** Inject a publisher that fails once: first `Review` errors post-completion; second `Verify(To=smoke)` should either republish or surface the unpublished-artifact condition rather than skip. Fix options: publish before the completed save (with rollback on failure), record a pending-publication flag consumed by Verify/flow, or reuse retained checkpoints for publication-only retries. --- ## Defended non-issues and resolved unknowns (each actively searched for counter-evidence) 1. **Swept-session resume does NOT wedge the sprint (context-pack unknown #1 resolved).** When a retained SessionID's store was swept (72h/2GiB), the production stack fails the "continue" StartRun with "session not found" (`missingSessionPolicy` stops retries), but agentwrap stamps `Validation.Configured` only via `withValidationMetadata`, which start failures bypass (agentwrap validation.go:260-263, 508-528) — so `runReviewer` takes its local fallback loop (review.go:974-1009), attempt 1 runs a full fresh-session re-run, and the coverage recovers at the cost of one wasted call. This is exactly the branch that execute lacks (cf. execute-resume-failure F1); review is structurally safe. 2. **PromptOnly blocked-path persists without the mutation lease** (review.go:437-441 vs lease guard at 424) — real inconsistency, unreachable today: no production caller sets `PromptOnly` (`prompt review` uses `PromptReview`, TUI/web use DryRun-free Review). Latent hazard only; flagged for whoever wires it. 3. **Fan-out liveness/races:** worker pool drains via buffered `done`/`sessions` channels with a single collector; late session events cannot regress terminal checkpoints (guard at review.go:828-830); `-race` clean over the suite; progressSaveErr accumulation instead of abort is intentional and terminally surfaced (608-611). 4. **Cancellation semantics:** ctx honored at prefix build, per-call boundaries, validators, and post-drain; cancellation wins over blocked-verdict persistence (613-617); prior artifact and LastComplete preserved on every non-completed terminal save (1270-1271). 5. **Crash window self-healing:** crash between `atomicWriteReview` and the completed save leaves Resume intact with all checkpoints completed, so the next plain rerun finishes with ZERO additional reviewer calls and rewrites the identical artifact — verified by trace; positive assurance property. 6. **Heartbeat sparsity is benign:** heartbeats land only on session-change/completion events, but `attemptExpired` checks PID liveness first (verify.go:471-473), live owners never expire themselves, cross-process reconcile is lease-blocked, and adoption refreshes OwnerPID on resumed runs (867-869). 7. **Snapshot `.complete` presence-trust:** benign given fingerprint-keyed directory names, lease-serialized writers, marker-written-last construction, and RemoveAll-rebuild on missing marker. 8. **Focus-mode cost hazard (documented behavior):** a focused run clears ActiveAttempt+Resume at its first running save (1241-1244), discarding an interrupted full run's validated checkpoints and retained sessions; correctness unaffected (LastComplete still gates focus admission), pure work-loss on a specific interleaving. 9. **Duplicate coverage IDs via slug collision** (two contracts whose names slugify identically) collapse checkpoints and fail closed at SaveFlowState validation — exotic trigger, fail-closed outcome. 10. **Severity sort is alphabetical, not rank order** ("blocker"<"high"<"info"<"low"<"medium"): deterministic and presentation-only; no consumer parses order. 11. **extractReviewJSON last-object-wins and O(n²) rescans:** consistent across AgentWrap validator and local fallback; whichever object wins must still pass the full decision table, so no trust transition changes; bounded inputs. 12. **PID-reuse staleness of lock/heartbeat ownership** is inherited from the shared locks/run-control surfaces and applies identically to all stages; out of scope here. EOF echo written && wc -l /home/antonioborgerees/coding/ultraplan/ultraplan-quality-gauntlet/review/jobs/review-sprint-conformance-review-failure/result.md

(A malicious governed input can also deliberately steer reviewers into the trap.) **Evidence / path.** 1. review.go:629-634 — `content := RenderReviewMarkdown(m, result)`; `if vf := ValidateReviewContent(content, m); len(vf) > 0 { … persistReviewFailure("generated review.md failed validation") }`. 2. index.go:218-221 — `strings.Contains(lower, "todo") || strings.Contains(lower, "tbd") || …`. 3. review.go:1094-1105 — findings rendered verbatim; 1083-1089 — input paths and changed paths rendered. 4. Reproduction: `GAUNTLET_MARKER=todo go test -overlay … -run TestGauntletMarkerFindingCompletion` → failed/artifact-invalid (see `evidence-probe-test.go.txt`); control marker → completed/pass_with_findings. 5. Contract context: TRD §18.6 does require review.md to contain "no placeholders", but the intent is unrendered-template detection (cf. planning validators); rejecting organic reviewer prose about real TODOs defeats the protocol's own requirement that actionable deviations be reported with citations (review-sprint-protocol; renderReviewerPrompt instructs findings to carry real citations). **Controls/counter-evidence searched.** No sanitization strips these substrings before render (`safeReviewText` redacts secrets/roots only). No test covers placeholder text inside findings — the `artifact-invalid` branch is untested and unreachable via the blocked path (blocked verdicts persist before render), which is why the trap survived. Result-level validation (`reviewResultProblems`) has no placeholder rule, proving acceptance upstream and rejection only at artifact level. Not fixable by operators short of rephrasing model outputs. **Regression test.** The attached probe: reviewer emits otherwise-valid low-severity direct finding mentioning "TODO"; assert `Review` completes and review.md passes `ValidateReviewContent`. Product fix options: restrict the final-artifact placeholder check to structural markers (template braces / literal ``) rather than English substrings, or apply it only to product-owned boilerplate sections, not model-authored text. --- ## F2 — Completed-review session deletion targets the wrong database; scoped runtime stores and `.ultra/cache/review` snapshots are reclaimed only by a sweep that finished sprints never trigger **Severity: low-medium · Confidence: high (mechanism verified end-to-end)** **Claim.** After success, `Review` deletes each completed session via `deleteCompletedSession` (review.go:657-659). For the production adapter this executes `agentwrap db "DELETE FROM event_sequence WHERE aggregate_id=…"` and `agentwrap session delete ` with env `append(os.Environ(), c.Agentwrap.Env...)` — no `OPENCODE_DB` (internal/platform/runtime/opencode.go:93-125, 180-184). But review sessions are created inside per-coverage scoped stores selected precisely by injecting `OPENCODE_DB` per request (service.go:1137-1139 → runtime.go:576-581 → agentwrap opencode/runtime.go:155-159). Deletion therefore runs against the default/global database, where these sessions do not exist: best-effort swallowed (`_ =`), it reclaims nothing while performing destructive SQL/VACUUM against an unrelated shared DB. **Observable bad outcome.** Every successful review leaves up to N retained stores (`projects/

/sprints//.ultraplan/runtime/opencode//opencode.db` with full transcripts) plus a complete `.ultra/cache/review/

///` snapshot copy. Reclamation depends solely on `CleanupRuntimeStores(sp.Path, 72h, 2GiB)` (runtime_metrics.go:119), which fires only when the NEXT runtime call admits work in that sprint — and snapshots are removed only on success (review.go:652), never on fail/cancel/blocked/crash paths. A sprint that ends after review leaks its stores and orphaned snapshot dirs (one per historical fingerprint) indefinitely; multi-sprint workspaces accumulate them without bound. **Trigger/preconditions.** Any completed review (stores); any failed/interrupted review or any superseded fingerprint (snapshots). **Evidence / path.** As cited above; store expiry conditions at store.go:211-227 require a subsequent `startSprintRuntime` call; snapshot removal only at review.go:652 (success) and rebuild-reset at 1613 (missing marker only). **Controls/counter-evidence searched.** `flow.go:37-42 deleteCompletedSessions` prefers whole-store deletion via `RuntimeStorePath` — but `Review` never uses it because completion state records sessions, not store paths. Errors being swallowed hides the mismatch. No TTL job exists for either location (grep across `internal/`). Verdict-fail intentionally retains sessions (review.go:654-656), compounding retention. **Regression test.** Adapter-level test: create a session under a scoped store (metadata `opencode.database_path`), call `DeleteSession`, assert rows removed from THAT database. Service-level test: after successful review with a fake deleter capturing the requested DB identity, assert deletion addresses the scoped store; add a lifecycle test asserting snapshot removal (or sweep) on terminal non-success outcomes. --- ## F3 — gitpublish failure after durable completion leaves review "completed" with no republication path; flow-level retry becomes a silent no-op and CLI retry pays a full fan-out **Severity: low · Confidence: high mechanism, medium impact** **Claim.** Terminal sequencing writes the artifact, then records completion durably (`saveReviewState(completed)`, clearing Resume and pinning digest/verdict), and only then publishes (review.go:636-651). If `publishReviewStage` fails, `Review` returns the error but durable state is already completed-with-matching-digest. Retry asymmetry follows: (a) `flow --to smoke`/`verify` treat the review as current (`currentReview := status.Review.Fresh && ExecutionStatus==completed…`, verify.go:65) and skip Review entirely — and unlike planning stages, which opportunistically republish on every flow pass (flow.go:149-155), there is no review republication outside `Review` itself; (b) the CLI `sprint … review` retry re-runs the entire bounded fan-out because Resume was cleared on the completed save, even though nothing about inputs changed. **Observable bad outcome.** Transient publisher failure (lock contention, hook rejection) yields a locally-complete review whose publication commit is missing from history; downstream flow operations proceed without it and never heal it; the operator's only cheap-looking remedy (`flow --to smoke`) silently does nothing, and the effective remedy re-spends every reviewer call. **Evidence / path.** review.go:644-651 ordering; verify.go:62-80 skip logic; flow.go:147-157 planning-stage republication asymmetry; resume cleared at review.go:1269. **Counter-evidence searched.** Direct CLI `review` rerun does republish — so recovery exists, but at full fan-out cost; smoke publishes harness/workspace paths but not `review.md` (publication.go:99-121). Digest/fingerprint checks make the local state self-consistent, so nothing detects the missing publication. **Regression test.** Inject a publisher that fails once: first `Review` errors post-completion; second `Verify(To=smoke)` should either republish or surface the unpublished-artifact condition rather than skip. Fix options: publish before the completed save (with rollback on failure), record a pending-publication flag consumed by Verify/flow, or reuse retained checkpoints for publication-only retries. --- ## Defended non-issues and resolved unknowns (each actively searched for counter-evidence) 1. **Swept-session resume does NOT wedge the sprint (context-pack unknown #1 resolved).** When a retained SessionID's store was swept (72h/2GiB), the production stack fails the "continue" StartRun with "session not found" (`missingSessionPolicy` stops retries), but agentwrap stamps `Validation.Configured` only via `withValidationMetadata`, which start failures bypass (agentwrap validation.go:260-263, 508-528) — so `runReviewer` takes its local fallback loop (review.go:974-1009), attempt 1 runs a full fresh-session re-run, and the coverage recovers at the cost of one wasted call. This is exactly the branch that execute lacks (cf. execute-resume-failure F1); review is structurally safe. 2. **PromptOnly blocked-path persists without the mutation lease** (review.go:437-441 vs lease guard at 424) — real inconsistency, unreachable today: no production caller sets `PromptOnly` (`prompt review` uses `PromptReview`, TUI/web use DryRun-free Review). Latent hazard only; flagged for whoever wires it. 3. **Fan-out liveness/races:** worker pool drains via buffered `done`/`sessions` channels with a single collector; late session events cannot regress terminal checkpoints (guard at review.go:828-830); `-race` clean over the suite; progressSaveErr accumulation instead of abort is intentional and terminally surfaced (608-611). 4. **Cancellation semantics:** ctx honored at prefix build, per-call boundaries, validators, and post-drain; cancellation wins over blocked-verdict persistence (613-617); prior artifact and LastComplete preserved on every non-completed terminal save (1270-1271). 5. **Crash window self-healing:** crash between `atomicWriteReview` and the completed save leaves Resume intact with all checkpoints completed, so the next plain rerun finishes with ZERO additional reviewer calls and rewrites the identical artifact — verified by trace; positive assurance property. 6. **Heartbeat sparsity is benign:** heartbeats land only on session-change/completion events, but `attemptExpired` checks PID liveness first (verify.go:471-473), live owners never expire themselves, cross-process reconcile is lease-blocked, and adoption refreshes OwnerPID on resumed runs (867-869). 7. **Snapshot `.complete` presence-trust:** benign given fingerprint-keyed directory names, lease-serialized writers, marker-written-last construction, and RemoveAll-rebuild on missing marker. 8. **Focus-mode cost hazard (documented behavior):** a focused run clears ActiveAttempt+Resume at its first running save (1241-1244), discarding an interrupted full run's validated checkpoints and retained sessions; correctness unaffected (LastComplete still gates focus admission), pure work-loss on a specific interleaving. 9. **Duplicate coverage IDs via slug collision** (two contracts whose names slugify identically) collapse checkpoints and fail closed at SaveFlowState validation — exotic trigger, fail-closed outcome. 10. **Severity sort is alphabetical, not rank order** ("blocker"<"high"<"info"<"low"<"medium"): deterministic and presentation-only; no consumer parses order. 11. **extractReviewJSON last-object-wins and O(n²) rescans:** consistent across AgentWrap validator and local fallback; whichever object wins must still pass the full decision table, so no trust transition changes; bounded inputs. 12. **PID-reuse staleness of lock/heartbeat ownership** is inherited from the shared locks/run-control surfaces and applies identically to all stages; out of scope here. Review complete. Result written to `review/jobs/review-sprint-conformance-review-failure/result.md` with the probe test preserved as evidence.

**Findings (failure/concurrency lens, frozen `c6f01cf`):**

- **F1 (medium-high, reproduced):** The final-artifact placeholder gate (`containsPlaceholder`, index.go:218-221) flags any `todo`/`tbd` substring in rendered review.md — including model-authored finding text. A valid review whose findings honestly report a TODO marker fails self-validation after all reviewers ran (`artifact-invalid: empty or placeholder review`), deterministically, on every rerun. Proven with an overlay-injected regression test (control marker completes; `todo` marker fails).
- **F2 (low-medium):** Post-success session deletion runs against the default OpenCode DB without the per-request `OPENCODE_DB` that created the sessions (opencode.go:93-125 vs runtime.go:576-581), so scoped stores and `.ultra/cache/review` snapshots are only reclaimed by a 72h sweep that finished sprints never trigger — indefinite leak.
- **F3 (low):** gitpublish failure after the durable completed save leaves no republication path: flow/verify skip the "current" review, planning-stage-style opportunistic republish doesn't exist for review, and CLI retry re-pays the full fan-out because Resume was cleared.

**Key non-issues defended:** swept-session resume self-heals via the local fresh-session fallback (agentwrap omits validation metadata on start failures — resolves context-pack unknown #1, and contrasts with execute's wedge); PromptOnly unlocked persist is unreachable today; heartbeat sparsity is dominated by PID-liveness checks; crash-before-completed-save self-heals with zero reviewer calls.

Note: `internal/workspace/skills.go` in the target checkout picked up an unrelated modification mid-session (not from me — all probing used `go test -overlay` writing only to `/tmp/opencode/probe`); left untouched and documented in the result.
